title: Devanagari — vowels and their signs
description: The eleven vowels, each in its stand-alone form and as the sign it becomes when attached to a consonant (shown on क). Learn the pairs: short and long i, short and long u.

cards.back: a, as the u in cup
cards.note: the inherent vowel — every consonant carries it unless another vowel sign replaces it

cards.back: ā, as the a in father
i, as in sit
ī, as the ee in seen
u, as in put
ū, as the oo in moon
ri, as in ritual
cards.note: rare; mostly in Sanskrit loans like ऋषि rishi

cards.back: e, as the a in gate
ai, as the a in bat
o, as in go
au, as the o in hot
ka — a bare consonant carries the short a
cards.note: the next cards show each vowel sign on this letter

cards.back: ā sign: a stroke after the letter
short i sign: a hook written before the letter
cards.note: written on the left but sounded after — the classic trap

cards.back: long ī sign: a hook after the letter
short u sign: a small curl below
long ū sign: a larger curl below
ri sign: a small hook below
e sign: one stroke above
ai sign: two strokes above
o sign: ā stroke plus one stroke above
au sign: ā stroke plus two strokes above
no vowel at all: a small slash below (virama / halant)
cards.note: used at the end of words and inside consonant clusters

cards.back: dot above (anusvara): nasalises, or stands for n/m before a consonant
moon-dot above (chandrabindu): a nasal vowel, as in French bon
two dots after (visarga): a light breath — rare, Sanskrit loans
